# Self-signed cert drift: mirror push fails x509 SAN mismatch

**Symptom:** `bootwright apply <target>` succeeds, but the Ansible mirror-push task fails with an x509 SAN mismatch error. The cert on disk was generated by a prior `bootwright secret sync` run.

**Root cause:** `bootwright secret sync` is idempotent — it reuses an existing cert file without regenerating it. If the desired `SelfSignedCertificateSpec` changed (different `commonName`, `dnsNames`, or `ipAddresses`) after the cert was first generated, the on-disk cert no longer matches. Ansible trusts the cert and attempts the push, only to discover the SAN mismatch at TLS handshake time deep inside the play.

**Fix:** `generatedSelfSignedDriftChecks` in `internal/cli/preflight.go` catches this at preflight and instructs the user to remove the stale cert pair and re-run `bootwright secret sync`.

**Remediation:** Remove `<secretsDir>/<name>` and `<secretsDir>/<name>.key`, then re-run `bootwright secret sync`.
